CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to assess the ongoing management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, with particular attention to medication efficacy and any emerging symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, expressing a mixture of progress and ongoing difficulties in his mental health journey. He reports that the increased dosage of lorazepam to 1 mg twice daily has provided him with more effective acute anxiety relief during stressful periods. However, he still experiences situational anxiety related to work deadlines, prompting him to seek additional therapeutic interventions.
Regarding his insomnia, Mr. Smith notes that while trazodone at 100 mg at bedtime continues to aid in sleep initiation, he has experienced a resurgence of nocturnal awakenings, now occurring approximately three times per night. He has initiated a sleep hygiene program, including reduced screen time before bed and a consistent sleep schedule, but still feels residual fatigue upon waking. He is interested in exploring melatonin at a higher dose or other adjunctive therapies if his sleep does not improve.
Mr. Smith reports that his tension-type headaches remain stable in frequency, still occurring twice a week, yet the intensity has fluctuated, with recent episodes reaching 7-8 out of 10 during particularly stressful work periods. He has been diligent in adhering to his ibuprofen regimen of 600 mg as needed, which he states provides moderate relief. He continues to maintain a headache diary, noting that stress appears to be a common trigger.
Persistent fatigue remains a concern for Mr. Smith, although he acknowledges some improvement in his energy levels since continuing bupropion 150 mg daily. He remains active in physical activities such as yoga and brisk walking, which he attributes to his overall wellness. However, he admits to experiencing occasional lapses in motivation, particularly during peak work stress.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 100 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 600 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 5. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 6. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 7. Lorazepam 1 mg twice daily as needed (increased) 8. Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime (continued) 9. Modafinil 100 mg in the morning (continued) 10. Bupropion 150 mg daily (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to engage in physical activities that support his mental health. He reports maintaining a balanced diet and has successfully reduced his caffeine intake. He actively participates in mindfulness and meditation practices, although he acknowledges that work-related stressors still present challenges to his overall well-being.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety is present but manageable; sleep quality has worsened; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency stable; intensity increased; no dizziness or visual disturbances noted. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue continues, though slightly improved; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/78 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented; appears mildly fatigued; mood appears stable with moderate anxiety. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with moderate anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Maintain lorazepam at 1 mg twice daily as needed for acute anxiety management. Discuss potential referral for CBT sessions to further enhance coping strategies. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 100 mg at bedtime. Consider a trial of melatonin 5 mg at bedtime if sleep quality does not improve further. Reassess sleep hygiene practices and potential need for additional interventions. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; maintain ibuprofen at 600 mg as needed. If headache intensity increases further, consider referral to a neurologist for comprehensive evaluation. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue bupropion at 150 mg daily; encourage consistent physical activity and reinforce stress management techniques.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-02-06 to evaluate symptom progression, medication efficacy, and address any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to continue documenting his symptoms and medication responses to facilitate ongoing management.
